haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports can make a row visible on the replica up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: The edit bumps updated_at, so a later nightly extract's 2-hour overlap window re-reads it, and the guarded MERGE applies it if newer.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at, which bumps updated_at. The warehouse keeps the row and sets is_deleted = true.
haiku-low.q5: The scheduler retries up to two more times, 15 minutes after each failure. After the third failure it pages on-call and hwm stays unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 and show only committed state, so they show the previous night's data. A staleness alert goes to #data-alerts with run_log status and attempt number.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation compares per-day counts and checksums for the last 30 days and reloads any mismatched day from the replica.
haiku-low.q8: The MERGE updates only when WHEN MATCHED AND s.updated_at >= t.updated_at, so older copies never overwrite newer ones. Identical rows are harmless no-ops.
haiku-low.q9: Stored as hwm in etl.control in the warehouse. Step 6 sets hwm = GREATEST(hwm, cutoff) in the same transaction as the merge, on commit. Cutoff is the replica's now(), taken once per attempt.
haiku-low.q10: The merge and the hwm advance commit in one warehouse transaction, and dashboards read only committed state, so they see the whole night or none of it.
haiku-low.q11: Staging is truncated at the start of the next attempt, so the failed staged rows are discarded. The retry re-reads hwm, so its window starts at the same hwm minus 2h, with a new cutoff.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads all that day's rows, including deleted ones, from the replica into stg.orders_recon and applies the same guarded MERGE. It does not touch hwm.

sonnet.q1: Scheduler cron at 02:00 UTC starts attempt 1. It extracts all columns of orders from the replica with updated_at > (hwm - 2h) and <= cutoff (replica now()), soft-deleted rows included.
sonnet.q2: The document does not explain why. It only says bulk imports can make a row visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at (hence the 2-hour lookback, 30 min margin). The cause is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q3: The edit bumps updated_at, so a later nightly window (updated_at > hwm-2h and <= cutoff) extracts it into staging, and the guarded MERGE updates dw.orders when s.updated_at >= t.updated_at.
sonnet.q4: The app never deletes; it sets deleted_at, which also bumps updated_at. The row is extracted like any change and merged; the warehouse keeps it with is_deleted = true (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).
sonnet.q5: The warehouse transaction rolls back or never started, hwm unchanged, run_log marked failed with error. Scheduler retries after 15 minutes (attempts 2 and 3, restarting from step 1, re-reading hwm). After the third failure on-call is paged; hwm stays, and the next night's window re-covers the gap. Staging is cleared by the next attempt.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 regardless and read only committed state, so they show the previous committed state (none of the night). The staleness watchdog posts an alert to #data-alerts with run_log status and attempt number (and on the third failure on-call is paged). A recovery note is posted if it commits later.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares per-day count and checksum for the last 30 days (by created_at) between replica and dw.orders, reloads mismatched days from the replica into stg.orders_recon, and applies the same guarded MERGE.
sonnet.q8: The MERGE updates a matched row only WHEN s.updated_at >= t.updated_at, so an older copy never overwrites a newer one; >= makes re-applying an identical row a harmless no-op. dw.orders has primary key order_id.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse, table etl.control (row orders_nightly, column hwm). It is set to GREATEST(hwm, cutoff), where cutoff is the replica's now() taken once per attempt, in the step 6 warehouse transaction, in the same transaction and commit as the MERGE.
sonnet.q10: The MERGE and the hwm/last_success_run_date update commit together in one warehouse transaction, and dashboards read committed state only, so they see the whole night or none of it.
sonnet.q11: Staging is truncated at the start of every attempt, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded and nothing is left behind. The retry re-reads hwm (unchanged since the failure) and extracts updated_at > hwm - 2h up to a new cutoff taken fresh on the replica; it never reuses the failed attempt's cutoff.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads all rows created (created_at) on each mismatched day from the replica, deleted ones included, into stg.orders_recon. It applies them with the same guarded MERGE into dw.orders in a warehouse transaction. It does not touch the nightly hwm.
